theme_central: The universality of the Qur'anic message: a group of jinn, having heard the Prophet's recitation, testify to its truth — Islam addresses every being endowed with reason, visible or invisible.
sources_note: 6-ruku structure sourced (al-islam.org, Commentary of Suratul Jinn): testimony of the jinn, oneness and resurrection, knowledge of the unseen in closing.

branches.title: The jinn testify
branches.resume: A group of jinn heard a wondrous recitation and recognized the oneness of Allah.

children.t: The jinn testify to having heard a wondrous, guiding recitation

branches.title: The guarded sky, diverse paths
branches.resume: The jinn recount finding the sky guarded by missiles; among them are the righteous and others astray.

children.t: The sky guarded by missiles since the revelation of the Qur'an
Among the jinn, righteous ones and others astray, diverse paths

branches.title: Trial by water, the mosques
branches.resume: Had they remained upright, Allah would have tested them with abundant water; the mosques belong to Allah alone.

children.t: Trial of abundant water, the mosques belong to Allah alone

branches.title: The Prophet's mission
branches.resume: The Prophet invokes only his Lord, possesses neither harm nor benefit for himself; a promise yet to come.

children.t: The Prophet only conveys the message, promise of the coming Judgment

branches.title: Knowledge of the unseen
branches.resume: Knowledge of the unseen reserved for Allah, except for whoever He approves among His messengers.

children.t: Knowledge of the unseen reserved for Allah, guard of angels around the messengers
